init.summary: Set up server roles, channels, and verification flow.
init.detail: Creates Onboarding, Rules, Documentation, Announcements, Meetings, and role-locked categories. Run once per server. Requires **/scrap** first if already initialized.

scrap.summary: Reset server to bare bones (one text, one voice channel).
scrap.detail: Removes all Granjur-created channels and roles. Use before re-running **/init**.

verify.summary: Verify your email (OTP) and enter holding.
verify.detail: Click **Request verification code**, enter your @granjur.com email, then enter the code sent to your email. Your nickname will be set from your email.

invite.summary: Send a server invite to an @granjur.com email.
invite.detail: Click **Enter email**, then submit the modal. Invite is sent by email and by DM if they are already on the server.

backlog.summary: View incoming users in holding and approve + assign roles.
backlog.detail: Select a user, then use the modal to enter roles (comma-separated) and optional notes. CEO/Server Manager only.

approve.detail: Step 1: Select user. Step 2: Select roles. Step 3: Confirm. Alternative to **/backlog**.

bug.detail: Select repo, enter title/description, optionally tag members. Creates a channel and optionally a GitHub issue.

ticket.detail: View tickets and update status. Senior Dev / CEO / Server Manager.

feature.detail: Enter title and description in the modal, then select repository or project.

schedule.detail: Enter topic and when (e.g. `2025-03-01 14:00` or `in 2 days`), then optionally select invitees.

project-db.summary: View or save project README/schema (project-level docs).
project-db.detail: Select a project to view its schema/README, or **New project** to paste and store. Use **/sql-dump** for versioned SQL dump history.

docs.summary: Browse, search and read the project documentation.
docs.detail: Browse by project or section and open a page, or pass `query` to search titles and page text. **Ticket docs** at the bottom of the first menu holds the write-ups attached to closed feature tickets, grouped by project. A page is rendered into an embed, long pages page with ◀ ▶, and pages that come from the documentation repository carry a link to the published site. Everything is read from the bot database, which a manager refreshes with **/setup** → **Sync docs now**.

explain.summary: Ask a question about a project; answered from its documentation with references.
explain.detail: Pick a project (or **No project** for all documentation) and ask in plain words. Claude reads that project's documentation on the server and answers with links to the pages it used. One question, one answer — ask again to follow up. Takes 30–90 seconds.

faq.detail: Ask: submit a question (optional repo). Search: query existing FAQs.

repos.detail: Add a repo with URL and optional project name. CEO/Server Manager.

dashboard.detail: Access admin modules. CEO or Server Manager only. The Tasks, Bugs and Features views carry a **project filter** — pick a project (or *No project*) to see only its work.

edit-docs.summary: Write a documentation page for a project, stored in the bot.
edit-docs.detail: Pick a project, then submit a page title and markdown body. The page is saved in the bot database and shows up in **/docs** under that project. It is not published to the documentation site, and a page synced from the documentation repository cannot be edited here — pick a different title if one already holds that address.

clock-in.summary: Start tracking your time against a task.
clock-in.detail: Pick the task you are working on, or **No task — general work**. You can pick your own tasks and any task in a project you belong to; leadership can pick any task. Clocking in on the task you are already on changes nothing and tells you how long it has run. Picking a different task stops the old timer and starts the new one in one step. Use **/clock-out** when you finish.

clock-out.detail: Stops your running timer and reports the session length and, for a task, that task's new total across everyone. Add an optional note about what you got done.

log-time.summary: Add time you already spent on a task.
log-time.detail: Log work you did without a timer. Duration takes **2h30m**, **90m**, **2.5h** or **1:30**; there is no maximum. **when** is the day the work ended: **today** (the default), **yesterday** or **YYYY-MM-DD** (UTC days). The entry ends at the current time of day on that date and runs backwards by the duration, and it cannot end in the future. You can pick your own tasks and any task in a project you belong to; leadership can pick any task, and **No task — general work** is always available. The reply shows the task's new total across everyone, and warns you if the entry overlaps another of yours. It is still saved, so check **/my-time**.

my-time.summary: See your tracked time, and fix or delete an entry.
my-time.detail: Shows your time for **today**, **this week** (the default), **this month** or **all time**: a running timer, a total per task, and your recent entries. Pick an entry from the list to **Edit** its duration, the day it ended or its note, or to **Delete** it. A running timer is stopped with **/clock-out**, not here. CEO and Server Manager can pass **person** to see, edit and delete someone else's entries; every change to time on a task is written to that task's activity log.

sql-dump.summary: Versioned SQL dumps per project schema (history, not project-db).
sql-dump.detail: Select a project schema, then view/search dump versions or submit a new dump. Use **/project-db** for project README/schema.

close-feature.summary: Close a feature ticket (only in a feature ticket channel).
close-feature.detail: Use only inside a feature ticket channel. Attach an MD file describing the feature implementation; the ticket is then closed and the doc is saved.

resolve-bug.summary: Resolve a bug ticket (only in a bug ticket channel).
resolve-bug.detail: Use only inside a bug ticket channel. Attach an MD file describing the solution; the ticket is then resolved and the doc is saved.

create-task.summary: Create a bug or feature task.
create-task.detail: Unified command for creating bugs and features. Select type, repo/project, fill in details, assign members.

update-task.summary: Update an existing task (status, scope, assignees, project, etc.).
update-task.detail: Run **/update-task** with nothing filled in to open the **Find a task** panel: pick a project, (CEO/Server Manager) pick a person, choose the task from the list, and its **task page** opens with everything you can change: **Edit details** (status, scope, assignees, title, description), **Test counts**, and dropdowns for project, implementation status and blockers (add or remove) — dropdown changes save as soon as you pick them. **Subtasks** opens a checklist: tick subtasks as finished, or add one (title, description, scope, assignees). A task cannot be finished while any subtask is open, and finishing the last subtask completes the task automatically; reopening a subtask reopens a finished task. Subtasks have no Discord channel of their own — their updates go in the parent's channel. Finished tasks are hidden until you press **Show finished**. To go straight to a task, type in the **task** field instead (it also searches by project, scope and person) and set any field as options — including blockers (**blocked_by**/**unblock**), **project**, and the API/QA/AC counts. CEO and Server Manager see and can update every task; everyone else only sees, and can only update, a task they hold (assigned to a feature, tagged on a bug); pasting an id that is not yours is refused the same as one that does not exist. Every change is recorded (who, what, when) and shown on the task's page in UBS Doc. Attaching a project makes the task show up under that project in **/dashboard**.

create-project-role.summary: Create or repair a project's role, and with it the project's whole private section.
create-project-role.detail: Type the name of an existing project (add new ones with **/projects** → Add project, which builds the section straight away). A project role only means something as the gate to its section, so this runs the same path as **/project-setup project:<project>**: the role, the `📂 PROJECT` category only that role can see, the ten section channels, the project's task channels moved in, and the role granted to everyone on **/project-members** and taken from everyone who is not. A managed job-role name such as `Database` is refused and nothing is created. Never deletes anything. CEO/Server Manager only.

create-project-categories.summary: Create or repair every project's private section — the same as /project-setup all:true.
create-project-categories.detail: Runs **/project-setup all:true**: for every project in this server, the project role, the `📂 PROJECT` category only that role can see, the ten section channels, the project's task channels moved in, and the role synced with **/project-members**. The reply grows project by project; a project the bot cannot touch is reported and the rest still run. Safe to re-run and never deletes anything. CEO/Server Manager only.

migrate.detail: Applies any unapplied SQL migration scripts. CEO/Server Manager only.

reconcile.summary: Sync members who joined while the bot was offline.
reconcile.detail: Scans all guild members, creates DB records for any missing, assigns the holding role, and notifies them to run **/verify**. CEO/Server Manager only.

meeting-channel.summary: Create a dedicated meeting voice + text channel pair.
meeting-channel.detail: Creates a linked voice and text channel for a meeting, and stores text messages in the meeting notes table with a user tag and timestamp. Pick a `project`, or run it inside one of a project's channels, and the meeting belongs to that project: its channels go in the project's section, visible only to its members. With no project the channels go in the public 📋 Meetings category. If the project has no section yet, or its section is full, the channels go to 📋 Meetings and the reply says why.

admin-panel.summary: Admin panel for viewing recordings, meetings, and members.
admin-panel.detail: Opens an admin-only panel with modules: Recordings (view meeting audio clips and file status), Meetings (scheduled meetings overview), Members (status summary and list). Administrator only.

cleanup.summary: Remove leftover channels not created by /init.
cleanup.detail: Finds and deletes orphan channels (leftover meeting channels, test channels, etc). Channels created by /init, /create-project-categories, and /create-channel are protected. CEO/Server Manager only.

create-channel.summary: Create a private voice + text channel pair.
create-channel.detail: Creates a voice and text channel visible only to designated members. These channels are tracked in the database and protected from /cleanup. Any verified member can use this.

playback.summary: Play back a meeting recording in a voice channel.
playback.detail: Select a meeting, then a recording to play in your current voice channel. Playback has Play/Pause, rewind 10s, forward 10s, and Stop controls. CEO/Server Manager only.

setup.detail: Run `/setup` with no options to view current settings. Set `timezone` (e.g. `America/New_York`, `Asia/Karachi`) so `/schedule` interprets meeting times correctly. CEO/Server Manager only.

meetings.summary: List, reschedule, or cancel your scheduled meetings.
meetings.detail: Shows your upcoming meetings. Select one to reschedule (new time) or cancel it. CEO/Server Manager can manage everyone's.

projects.summary: List projects, add a project, link a repository
projects.detail: CEO/Server Manager only. A project's docs folder determines which UBS-Doc pages are attributed to it.

project-members.summary: Add, remove, or list who works on a project.
project-members.detail: Run it inside a project's channels and **project** can be left out: it is the project whose section you are in. Anywhere else, start typing in the **project** field and pick from the suggestions. **add** sets a member's role (Lead, Developer, Backend Developer, Frontend Developer, QA, Design; default Developer) and gives them the project's role, so they can see its channels. Using it again on someone already on the project changes their role. **remove** takes them off and takes the project role away. **add** and **remove** also post the change in the project's members channel and refresh its pinned list. **list** shows members grouped by role, plus anyone else currently holding a task on the project. This is the list the UBS-Doc site shows.

project-setup.summary: Create or repair a project's Discord section — its role, category and channels.
project-setup.detail: Gives the project a role, a `📂 PROJECT` category only that role can see, the ten section channels (members, documentation, meetings, meeting voice, and chat + voice for frontend, backend and database), and moves the project's task channels in. Safe to re-run: it repairs what is missing and never deletes anything. Pass **project** for one project or **all:true** for every project in the server — a project the bot cannot touch is reported and the rest still run. **preview:true** prints the plan and changes nothing. It also grants the project role to everyone on **/project-members** and takes it from everyone who is not.
